findings.title: #5 gravipack.fr, the audited domain, has no indexed pages, and the store's indexed URLs are split between gravipack.com and www.gravipack.com
findings.description:
Context first: gravipack.fr, the domain submitted for this audit, is not where the brand's indexed store lives. We sampled search results from a US-located, non-Google index (about 60 phase-1 queries plus phase-2 checks). In them, site:gravipack.fr, "gravipack.fr", "www.gravipack.fr" and "gravipack.fr" sac à dos returned no URL on gravipack.fr or www.gravipack.fr. Every official result was on gravipack.com.

Every third-party page that names a domain also names gravipack.com: the Trustpilot profile (/review/gravipack.com), the LinkedIn company page, Les Pépites Tech and Motherbase. The legal notice at gravipack.com/mentions-legales/ (publisher EXOSQUELETTE LIGHT, host Gandi) describes gravipack.com, and no link or mention profile was found for gravipack.fr.

We could not fetch the live sites from the audit sandbox, and a PageSpeed request for gravipack.fr failed with a quota error (HTTP 429). So it is unknown whether .fr redirects, is parked or has lapsed. Zero indexed pages is exactly what a correct 301 from .fr to .com produces, so the .fr part is Low unless the on-site check shows .fr is parked, lapsed, not resolving or serving duplicate 200 pages. In those cases it becomes Medium, and higher if gravipack.fr is printed on packaging, in press kits or on old campaign material.

Second, the gravipack.com store appears on both hosts in the results we sampled. Of the 114 owned URLs observed, 58 were on www.gravipack.com, 40 on gravipack.com (apex) and 16 on the legacy presta.gravipack.com, which has its own finding. These counts describe the URLs we saw, not the size of the index.
- Apex: the home page, /boutique-gravipack/, /mentions-legales/, /conditions-generales-de-vente/, /contacts/, /nos-engagements/ and most product categories: /categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/ and its randonnée, scolaire, business, voyage, urbain, militaire, outillage and claie-de-portage children.
- www: /faq/, /contact-gravipack/, /articles/, /actualites-gravipack-2/, the /categorie/* blog archives, /a-propos-de-nous-gravipack-au-service-de-votre-dos/, /gravipackers/, the attribute and tag archives, and 28 of the 46 product URLs (18 were on apex).
- Pages from the same listing sit on different hosts. The shop root is on apex, while /boutique-gravipack/page/2/ and /boutique-gravipack/?order=price are on www. /categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/ is on apex and its /page/2/ on www.
- For the brand query 'gravipack', the owned results alternated between hosts: www /gravipackers/, apex /, a www product, then apex /nos-engagements/. For 'gravipack prix', apex /boutique-gravipack/ (#4) was followed by www /boutique-gravipack/?order=price (#5).

No product or category path was recorded on both hosts; only the home page was reported on both. This is mixed-host indexing, not proven duplication. It fits either of two explanations:
- Both hosts answer 200 without consistent canonicals.
- A redirect already exists and this non-Google index still holds stale entries. This is plausible, because WordPress's redirect_canonical() and Yoast/Rank Math normally enforce one host.

Some examples first reported as host duplicates (Light Promax, G-Pack) are really different slugs and are handled in the duplicate-product-URL finding.

Why it matters: A brand should have one 'entity home': a single host that Google, Merchant Center and AI answer engines all treat as official.

If both hosts answer 200, Google treats them as separate URLs. It has to cluster them and may pick a canonical you did not choose. Search Console data is split if only a URL-prefix property is verified, and Merchant Center expects feed landing pages on the claimed website.

For gravipack.fr, the stakes are brand protection and type-in traffic, because French customers and journalists naturally guess '.fr'. A parked, lapsed or duplicate .fr wastes those visits and blurs the brand entity. A lapsed registration could also be taken by a third party.

Effect on SEO: If both .com hosts serve 200, internal links and external equity are split between them. Crawl is spent on duplicate fetches, updates are re-clustered more slowly, and results can show a non-preferred URL with an older title. A clean single-hop 301 consolidates everything on one host and gives knowledge-graph and AI systems one official URL.

For .fr, a correct path-preserving 301 already delivers the full benefit. No link profile was found for .fr, so the 'wasted link equity' effect is small, and the main gains are type-in traffic and brand consistency. If .fr instead serves duplicate 200 pages, it becomes a cross-domain duplicate that competes with .com.

Impact 6/10 · Effort Low · Confidence needs-on-site-check
findings.recommendation: 0. **Measure before choosing. Do not pick a host from this report.** Find which host is canonical today and keep it unless there is a strong reason to switch: - WordPress: Réglages → Général → 'Adresse web de WordPress (URL)' and 'Adresse web du site (URL)', or `wp option get home` and `wp option get siteurl`. - View the source of the home page and one product page on both hosts. Note which host `rel=canonical` and `og:url` use. - Open the Yoast or Rank Math sitemap (`/sitemap_index.xml`) and note the host in the `<loc>` entries. - In Search Console, run URL Inspection on about 10 URLs from each host and compare 'Canonical déclarée par l'utilisateur' with 'Canonical sélectionnée par Google'. www may well be the current canonical, since most products, the FAQ and most posts were observed there. Forcing apex would then be a second migration. Trustpilot's 'review/gravipack.com' is not evidence for apex, because Trustpilot always strips 'www'. 1. **Run the redirect matrix** (see onsite_check). If every non-canonical variant already returns a single 301 to the same path on the canonical host, add no rules. The mixed index is stale, so go to step 5. 2. **If both .com hosts return 200, find the layer responsible before adding rules.** WordPress's redirect_canonical() normally redirects any host that does not match 'home'. If it does not, check: - a page cache serving copies per host (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Varnish); - a CDN or proxy (e.g. Cloudflare) rewriting the Host header or carrying its own redirect rules; - the vhost configuration. Stacking an .htaccess rule on top of an existing CDN or plugin redirect is the usual cause of redirect loops and chains. 3. **Take a full backup (files and database) and work in a maintenance window** before touching 'home' or 'siteurl'. A mismatch between the database and the server rules can lock you out of wp-admin; you can recover by defining `WP_HOME` and `WP_SITEURL` in wp-config.php. Then add one server-level rule **above** `# BEGIN WordPress` that sends every variant to the canonical host in one hop. The example below assumes www is canonical. If apex wins, match `^www\.gravipack\.com$` instead and target https://gravipack.com/. ```apache RewriteEngine On # gravipack.fr, www.gravipack.fr and the non-canonical .com host -> one hop RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^(www\.)?gravipack\.fr$ [NC,OR] RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^gravipack\.com$ [NC] RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://www.gravipack.com/$1 [R=301,L] # http -> https on the canonical host (behind a proxy/CDN test X-Forwarded-Proto instead of %{HTTPS}) RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://www.gravipack.com/$1 [R=301,L] ``` Nginx equivalent: ```nginx server { listen 80; listen 443 ssl; server_name gravipack.fr www.gravipack.fr gravipack.com; # certificate must cover all names return 301 https://www.gravipack.com$request_uri; } server { listen 80; server_name www.gravipack.com; return 301 https://www.gravipack.com$request_uri; } ``` 4. **Clean internal references once the redirect works:** - Run Better Search Replace as a dry run, then live, replacing the non-canonical host with the canonical one in `wp_posts` and `wp_postmeta`. Skip the `guid` column, and never edit home or siteurl this way. - If the site uses Elementor, run Elementor → Outils → Remplacer l'URL. - Fix menu links, then purge the page cache and the CDN. 5. **Align every signal on the canonical host:** - Yoast or Rank Math outputs an absolute, self-referencing canonical. - The XML sitemap lists canonical-host URLs only. - robots.txt contains `Sitemap: https://<hôte-canonique>/sitemap_index.xml`. - The `url` in the Organization and WebSite JSON-LD uses the canonical host. - Merchant Center feed `link` values match the claimed website. 6. **Search Console and Bing:** - Create a **Domain property** for gravipack.com (DNS TXT record). It covers www, apex, presta, http and https. - Create a separate Domain property for gravipack.fr. - Resubmit the sitemap. - In Bing Webmaster Tools, import from Search Console or verify by DNS. - Allow 2-4 weeks for Google to re-cluster before judging the result. 7. **gravipack.fr:** - Confirm ownership at the registrar and switch on multi-year auto-renewal. - Make sure https://gravipack.fr and https://www.gravipack.fr carry a valid TLS certificate. A redirect behind a certificate error never reaches users. - Make both return a path-preserving 301 to the canonical .com host in **one hop**. The rule in step 3 covers this if .fr points to the same server. Registrar 'web forwarding' is acceptable only if it issues a 301, keeps the path and serves HTTPS. - Do **not** add hreflang between .fr and .com. Both are French for France, and hreflang is only for distinct language or region versions. - Use the Change of Address tool only if .fr ever hosted the site. - Do not move the store to .fr: all observed equity is on .com. 8. **Off-site:** use the exact canonical URL everywhere you control it: - LinkedIn, the YouTube 'À propos' tab, and the Instagram and Facebook bios; - the claimed Trustpilot business profile; - the GRAVIPACK seller profile on Decathlon; - a final news update on each of the 4 KissKissBankBank campaigns (KKBB support now redirects to Ulule, so post these updates yourself); - the press kit, email signatures and packaging.

findings.title: #7 The same products are indexed under several URLs, including a second /produit-gravipack/ base and duplicated slugs and titles
findings.description:
In the search results we sampled, several product families appear under more than one URL. Some of these URLs use a second product base, /produit-gravipack/, alongside WooCommerce's /produit/.
- **Sherpa Kaki ×3**, all with the same 90-character title ('Sac léger avec exosquelette anti mal de dos de montagne Sherpa Kaki Gravipack anti douleur'): www /produit/sac-a-dos-sherpa-kaki-avec-exosquelette-…-legerete-en-haute-montagne/, apex /produit-gravipack/sac-a-dos-sherpa-kaki and apex /produit-gravipack/sac-a-dos-sherpa.
- **Hiking Terracotta ×2**, with the same title: www /produit/sac-a-dos-revolutionnaire-anti-mal-de-dos-de-randonnee-hiking-terracotta-…/ and apex /produit-gravipack/sac-a-dos-revolutionnaire.
- **Light Promax ×3**, all surfacing for a single query:
  - apex /produit/sac-a-dos-porte-outil-anti-douleur-avec-exosquelette-light-promax-gravipack/ and www /produit/sac-a-dos-exosquelette-outillage-light-promax-gravipack-anti-mal-de-dos/, both titled 'Sac à dos outillage anti-douleur exosquelette Gravipack®';
  - www /produit/sac-anti-mal-de-dos-exosquelette-outillage-parcours-gravipack/ ('… Light Promax de Gravipack').
- **Cargo Max ×2**, with the identical title 'Claie de portage aluminium exosquelette Gravipack pour charges lourdes'.
- **Business Talk V4 ×3**, surfacing for one query: a 20 L page plus two 25 L pages (…-25l-…-pour-deux-ordinateurs-…-revolutionnaire/ and …-ordinateur-25l-…-ergonomie-eva-memoire-de-forme/). The 20 L page may be a distinct SKU; the two 25 L pages are the likely duplicate pair.
- **Kingston ×2**: /produit/sac-a-dos-teletravail-kingston-…/ and /produit/vive-la-rentree-scolaire-…-kingston-avec-exosquelette/. Both ranked together (#1 and #3) for 'sac à dos scolaire anti mal de dos' in the extended sample.
- **Solar battery ×2**, one slug ending in '-copie' (a leftover from WooCommerce's 'Dupliquer' action).
- **Pearl**: /produit/…pearl-29l-gris…/ and /produit-gravipack/sac-a-dos-exosquelette-gravipack-pearl/ carry **different** titles; the second says 'Pearl femme'. This may be a separate listing or an old version.

Corrections:
- The two G-Pack URLs (collège/lycée on apex, 'pour la journée … professionnels et vélo' on www) share the title 'Sac à dos exosquelette révolutionnaire et unique G-Pack Gravipack', but may be two real products. In that case the problem is a duplicate title, not a duplicate URL.
- The Compostelle 65 L '-copie' slug is a different capacity and belongs to the slug finding.
- One URL per colour (Sherpa bleu, Sherpa 45L orange and Sherpa kaki; Hiking 30L gris and Hiking terracotta; Oslo rouge; Pearl 29L gris) is a pattern Google supports with ProductGroup markup, so it is not a defect in itself.
- The short /produit-gravipack/ URLs may already be 301s or shortlinks that a stale, non-Google index still lists.
- Real ranking cannibalisation can only be confirmed in Search Console (query → pages).

The earlier High rating rested on an 'unverifiable' verdict, which does not meet the evidence rule, so this is Medium until the status check is done.

Why it matters: Each live duplicate of a product splits its links, reviews, internal links and engagement. Google then chooses for itself which URL to show, and may pick the weaker copy or one with an old title.

Duplicate titles across products also make the catalogue look careless. They make it harder for the official product page to win model queries, where in the sampled results marketplaces already rank above it.

Effect on SEO: Model queries ('gravipack sherpa', 'light promax', 'business talk') are spread over sibling URLs, so no single page builds full strength. Search Console is likely to show 'Doublon : Google n'a pas choisi la même URL canonique que l'utilisateur' or 'Autre page avec balise canonique correcte' at scale (to verify). Review stars and merchant listings may attach to inconsistent URLs or prices.

Consolidating with 301s, or grouping real variants with ProductGroup markup, concentrates the signals on one URL per product.

Impact 6/10 · Effort Medium · Confidence needs-on-site-check
findings.recommendation: 1. **Audit status first.** - Crawl every URL in the groups with Screaming Frog in list mode, or run `curl -sI` on each. Record the status, final URL, rel=canonical and `<title>`. - Export the products (Produits → Exporter, CSV with ID, SKU, slug, status and GTIN) to separate distinct SKUs from copies. - Check each URL with Search Console URL Inspection. Only URLs answering 200 count as duplicates; a URL that already 301s is not one. 2. **Find what produces /produit-gravipack/.** Possible sources: - an old 'Base des produits' under Réglages → Permaliens; - a custom rewrite (`wp rewrite list | grep produit-gravipack`); - a shortlink or redirect plugin (Pretty Links, Redirection, Rank Math Redirections); - an .htaccess rule. If these URLs answer 200, add explicit 301s to the surviving /produit/ URLs one by one, because the slugs differ (e.g. /produit-gravipack/sac-a-dos-sherpa-kaki → /produit/sac-a-dos-sherpa-kaki-avec-…/). Then remove the source. 3. **True copies (same SKU):** - Keep the URL with the most links, sales and reviews (Search Console Links and Performance). - 301 the others to it with Redirection or Rank Math → Redirections (type 301). - Move the reviews by reassigning them to the survivor's product ID (WooCommerce reviews are comments). - Update menus and internal links. - Only then move the copy to the Corbeille and empty it. Likely candidates: Sherpa Kaki ×3, Hiking Terracotta ×2, Light Promax ×3, Cargo Max ×2, the two Business Talk V4 25 L pages and the '-copie' battery. 4. **Distinct SKUs that share a title** (G-Pack ×2, Business Talk V4 20 L vs 25 L, and the two Pearl pages if both are real): give each one a title and H1 that state the difference, and keep a self-referencing canonical. For example: - « Business Talk V4 20 L – sac à dos ordinateur à exosquelette | Gravipack » - « Business Talk V4 25 L – sac à dos 2 ordinateurs à exosquelette | Gravipack » - « G-Pack collège-lycée – sac à dos scolaire à exosquelette » - « G-Pack pro & vélo – sac à dos de journée à exosquelette » For Kingston, decide whether 'Vive la rentrée scolaire' is a real separate school offer; if not, 301 it to the Kingston product. 5. **Colour variants: choose ONE model and apply it to every family.** - **(A) Single page:** make it a WooCommerce variable product (Type de produit : Produit variable; attribute Couleur used for variations). Colour selection then uses `?attribute_pa_couleur=kaki` on the parent URL. 301 the old colour URLs to the parent. - **(B) Multi-page:** keep one self-canonical URL per colour and group the URLs with ProductGroup markup, using the same `item_group_id` in the Merchant Center feed. Do **not** canonicalise colour pages to the parent while also submitting them as landing pages; that sends conflicting signals. Example for (B); check that Rich Results Test reports valid merchant listings: ```json {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"ProductGroup","name":"Gravipack Sherpa 45 L","productGroupID":"SHERPA45","variesBy":["https://schema.org/color"],"brand":{"@type":"Brand","name":"Gravipack"}, "hasVariant":[ {"@type":"Product","sku":"SHERPA45-KAKI","name":"Gravipack Sherpa 45 L kaki","color":"kaki","url":"https://<hôte>/produit/<slug-kaki>/","image":"https://<hôte>/…/sherpa-kaki.jpg","offers":{"@type":"Offer","price":"<prix>","priceCurrency":"EUR","availability":"https://schema.org/InStock"}}, {"@type":"Product","sku":"SHERPA45-BLEU","name":"Gravipack Sherpa 45 L bleu","color":"bleu","url":"https://<hôte>/produit/<slug-bleu>/"} ]} ``` With either option, the /produit-gravipack/ URLs and the true copies need 301s, not just canonicals. 6. **One migration map, one release.** Combine these 301s with the presta map and any slug changes (such as the Compostelle 65 L '-copie' slug, handled in the slug finding) so that no redirect chains form. Regenerate the Yoast or Rank Math sitemap so it lists only the surviving URLs, then re-crawl to confirm there are no duplicate product titles.

findings.title: #16 The legacy PrestaShop store presta.gravipack.com still appears in search results with old product, study and award pages
findings.description:
The old PrestaShop store at presta.gravipack.com still appears in the search results we sampled (a US-located, non-Google index). We recorded 16 URLs on it:
- **Home page**, titled 'Gravipack, le sac a dos scolaire, business et randonnée, ce sac à dos allègent le poids…' (126 characters).
- **Categories:** /2-accueil, /22-produit, /24-sac-a-dos-sport, /72-sac-a-dos-scolaire and /73-gravipack ('Gravipack, le sac à dos en apesanteur qui ne fait pas mal au dos et aux épaules').
- **/40-etude-scientifique-soulage-le-dos-gravipack** ('L'étude scientifique du sac à dos en apesanteur Gravipack.'). This is the only indexed page about the 2019 LBMC / Faculté de Médecine Lyon-Sud study that we found.
- **Other pages:** /59-concours-lepine-medaille-argent-meilleur-sac-a-dos-gravipack, /plan-du-site-gravipack, and /content/1-livraison-sac-a-dos-gravipack ('… Gravipack le meilleur sac a dos au monde - livraison client').
- **Six product pages:**
  - Safar Vibe (/accueil/13-…)
  - Business Talk (/accueil/15-…)
  - Hiking33 (/accueil/16-sac-a-dos-gravipack-hikking33.html, 'Le seul sac à dos au monde qui allège le poids Hiking 33 Gravipack.')
  - Road Adventure (/accueil/17-…)
  - Sherpa 45 (/accueil/19-…, '… Le meilleur sac à dos de montagne.')
  - Feather (/accueil/21-…)

The legacy pages still compete for the brand's own model queries in the results we sampled:
- **'gravipack hiking 33':** presta was #8 in one run. In a re-run it was #9, and the main store was absent from the top 10.
- **'gravipack feather cartable':** presta was #10 and the only owned result.
- **'gravipack business talk':** presta was #9.
- **'gravipack prix':** the presta home page was #9.
- **site:gravipack.com searches** (categorie-produit, sac business ordinateur, CGV livraison, presse Lépine) also returned presta URLs. A gravipack.com-restricted 'Feather … prix' search returned 8 presta URLs out of 12.

The pages carry crowdfunding-era model names. Feather, Road Adventure and Safar Vibe exist only there among the owned sites, and 'Hiking 33' and 'Business Talk' differ from today's 'Hiking 30L / Terracotta' and 'Business Talk V4'. They also carry superlatives ('le seul sac à dos au monde', 'le meilleur sac à dos de montagne', 'en apesanteur') that the claims findings ask to retire.

On prices:
- One phase-2 snippet showed the Feather page at 149,00 € TTC 'en stock', although Feather was not found on the main store. That page may be presenting an offer that no longer exists.
- The other legacy prices, the 'commandes de réservation 2-3 mois' wording and the delivery terms came from search summaries that were not saved, so they are not asserted here.
- 249 € was still the regular Sherpa price in 2026. Decathlon's 149,90 € promotion ran 18/06-30/08/2026 and has ended, so the legacy Sherpa price is not stale.

Whether these URLs still return 200, already redirect or return 404 could not be checked, and indexes lag behind redirects. Hence Medium; raise to High if curl shows presta still serving 200 pages.

Why it matters: A second storefront for the same brand competes with the live store for brand and model queries, and for some of them it is the first owned result. Buyers researching a model therefore meet stale content: retired model names, superlatives the brand is moving away from, and possibly lapsed offers.

The old store also holds two assets the main site needs: the study summary and the Concours Lépine page. AI answer engines can quote the legacy pages as current facts.

Effect on SEO: Links and relevance earned during the crowdfunding years (2019-2021 press, KissKissBankBank) stay on the legacy host and do not reach gravipack.com. Model queries ('gravipack hiking 33', 'gravipack feather') show a legacy page instead of the live product. Crawl budget is spent on a retired store. Prices or availability that differ across the brand's own URLs add risk for merchant listings.

Clean one-to-one 301s pass these signals to the live equivalents and remove the stale results.

Impact 5/10 · Effort Medium · Confidence needs-on-site-check
findings.recommendation: 1. **Check the live state.** Run `curl -sI` on the 16 URLs and the presta root (see onsite_check). Find out whether PrestaShop still takes orders. If it does, set a shutdown date and export orders and customers according to your retention obligations. 2. **Prioritise by equity.** In the gravipack.com Search Console Domain property (see the host finding), filter Links and Performance on 'presta.' to see which legacy URLs have links or impressions. Use Bing Webmaster Tools as a second source. 3. **Move the unique content first. Do not return 410 for it.** - Publish the study summary on gravipack.com, as described in the evidence-page finding: protocol, authors, sample and exactly what the 92 % measures, after legal review. Redirect /40-etude-scientifique-soulage-le-dos-gravipack only once that page is live, and send it straight there. - Merge the useful facts from /59-concours-lepine-… (medal, year, category) into the existing /gravipack-le-sac-anti-mal-de-dos-prime-au-concours-lepine/ post. 4. **Map URL by URL to pages that exist today on the canonical host.** Do not map to planned URLs such as /cartable-ergonomique/, which would create 404s or later chains. Take the final product URLs from the duplicate-product finding. Suggested map: - `/` → home page - `/2-accueil` → /boutique-gravipack/ - `/22-produit` and `/73-gravipack` → /categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/ - `/72-sac-a-dos-scolaire` → …/sac-a-dos-exosquelette-anti-mal-de-dos-scolaire-college-lycee-et-etudiant/ - `/24-sac-a-dos-sport` → …/sac-a-dos-exosquelette-anti-mal-de-dos-de-randonnee-montagne-trek-compostelle/ - Sherpa 45 → the surviving Sherpa product URL - Hikking33 → the Hiking 30L / Terracotta product - Business Talk → Business Talk V4 (a current product) - Feather → the Feather page if it is re-listed on gravipack.com, otherwise the scolaire category - `/content/1-livraison-…` → /conditions-generales-de-vente/, or a dedicated delivery page if one exists - `/59-concours-lepine-…` → the Lépine post - `/40-etude-scientifique-…` → the new evidence page (step 3) - Safar Vibe, Road Adventure and `/plan-du-site-gravipack` → the closest category if they have links or impressions, otherwise **410 Gone** - Never send unmapped URLs to the home page. Google treats mass redirects to the home page as soft 404s. 5. **Implement the map at server level on the presta vhost, not inside PrestaShop.** Replace PrestaShop's .htaccess with explicit rules. The host below is an example; use the canonical host from the host finding. ```apache RewriteEngine On RewriteRule ^$ https://www.gravipack.com/ [R=301,L] RewriteRule ^2-accueil/?$ https://www.gravipack.com/boutique-gravipack/ [R=301,L] RewriteRule ^(22-produit|73-gravipack)/?$ https://www.gravipack.com/categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/ [R=301,L] RewriteRule ^72-sac-a-dos-scolaire/?$ https://www.gravipack.com/categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/sac-a-dos-exosquelette-anti-mal-de-dos-scolaire-college-lycee-et-etudiant/ [R=301,L] RewriteRule ^59-concours-lepine- https://www.gravipack.com/gravipack-le-sac-anti-mal-de-dos-prime-au-concours-lepine/ [R=301,L] RewriteRule ^accueil/16-sac-a-dos-gravipack-hikking33\.html$ https://www.gravipack.com/produit/<slug-hiking>/ [R=301,L] # ... one line per mapped URL ... RewriteRule ^accueil/13-sac-a-dos-gravipack-safar-vibe\.html$ - [G,L] # anything left: 410, never the home page RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !^/robots\.txt$ RewriteRule ^ - [G,L] ``` On Nginx, use a `map $uri $presta_target { … }` with `if ($presta_target) { return 301 $presta_target; } return 410;`. 6. **Keep the redirects reachable:** - Keep presta.gravipack.com in DNS, keep its vhost and keep a valid TLS certificate for at least 12 months, ideally permanently. - Switch off the PrestaShop application, not the host. If the back office must stay online, put it behind HTTP authentication on a separate path. - Do not Disallow presta in robots.txt and do not noindex it. Google has to recrawl the URLs to see the 301s. - Use the Removals tool only as a temporary cover if a stale price or claim is causing harm; it hides URLs for about 6 months only. - Optionally, submit a temporary sitemap listing the 16 legacy URLs to speed up recrawl. Remove it once they show 'Page avec redirection'. 7. **Update the links you control** to their gravipack.com equivalents: post a final news update on each of the 4 KissKissBankBank campaigns, and update old press releases and social bios. Keep this presta map in the single URL-migration sheet shared with the slug and product-merge work. That way a later slug change updates these targets directly and does not create chains.

findings.title: #28 Other brand storefronts and hosts (gravipack.ma, gravipacker.com, a probable agency staging host) show different catalogues, model names and prices
findings.description:
Besides gravipack.com and the legacy presta host, the search results we sampled surfaced three more hosts carrying the brand. None of them has a visible relationship to the main store.

1. **gravipack.ma is a second 'Gravipack®' storefront.**
   - It ranked #1, and its /categories-de-produits/sac-a-dos-bureautique/ page #7, for 'Gravipack sac à dos revendeur boutique'. That query was run with gravipack.com and the big retailers excluded.
   - Searches restricted to .ma returned the home page, /categories-de-produits/sac-a-dos-bureautique/, /product-category/sac-a-dos-gravipack/gravipack-edition-outdoor/ and /product-category/gravipack-accessoire/accessoires-high-tech-bureautique/.
   - Prices are in **euros**: Rome 119.90, Dublin 249.90, Trek Air 25L 129, Sherpa Peak 50L 189 (range about 119-249.90 €).
   - It promises 'livraison rapide partout dans le monde', which overlaps the French market.
   - Some model names do not exist on gravipack.com (Trek Air 25L, Summit Air 35L, Sherpa Peak 50L, against Sherpa 45 and Hiking 30L). Others are shared (Rome, Dublin).
   - Its bureautique page shows a 1-year warranty.
   - It uses two category URL bases (/categories-de-produits/ and /product-category/), and one page says 'boutique en préparation'.
   - We do not know who operates it or whether it is meant as a Moroccan regional store. The brand does have Moroccan press coverage (lematin.ma, challenge.ma, fnh.ma).
2. **gravipacker.com is a third brand domain** (#5 in the same sample). It shows the old Vincennes (94300) address with contact@gravipack.com and pages about test events. The registered seat has been 10 rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris since 19/05/2026.
3. **gravipack.archemia.fr is probably a development or staging host.**
   - It appeared only as the subject of a ScamAdviser report (scamadviser.com/fr/verifier-site/gravipack.archemia.fr, rated 'probably legitimate'). That report ranked #9 for 'gravipack arnaque' in one run.
   - A direct search for the host returned no page from it.
   - Archemia is a communication and web-development agency in Nanterre (Sortlist profile, about 5 people, founded 2023).
   - The duplicate-content risk is speculative, so this is a Low sub-item. The only effect we observed is a scam-checker page carrying the brand name in an 'arnaque' result.

International note (Info): we found no English or other-language Gravipack-owned URL, although demand signals exist: the English KissKissBankBank campaign page, a 2021 English translation on gearxnews (weak), and the Moroccan press. The phase-1 conclusion 'no regional version, hreflang not applicable' is therefore partly contradicted by gravipack.ma. hreflang only becomes relevant if .ma is meant to be the Moroccan version of the same catalogue.

Why it matters: Every domain carrying the brand needs one declared role. Two stores selling the same brand in the same language and currency to overlapping markets compete as duplicates, unless they are clearly regional and cross-annotated.

Buyers and AI engines also cannot tell which shop, model names, prices and warranty are official. That adds to the trust doubts already visible in the 'avis' and 'arnaque' results.

Merchant Center ties offers to one claimed website per account and country. A crawlable staging copy duplicates content and leaks unfinished pages.

Effect on SEO: Brand and model signals split across domains. gravipack.ma pages can appear in French results next to the official store with different names and prices, and entity facts (address, warranty, model names) conflict across the brand's own sites.

The fix has three parts:
- either hreflang fr-FR / fr-MA backed by real regional differences, or consolidation by 301;
- one list of official domains;
- the staging host behind authentication.
Together they concentrate equity on gravipack.com and remove the conflicting shopping entities.

Impact 4/10 · Effort Medium · Confidence likely
findings.recommendation: 1. **Inventory and ownership.** - Check WHOIS and the legal notices of gravipack.ma and gravipacker.com to confirm who runs them: EXOSQUELETTE LIGHT, a licensee or a distributor. - Ask Archemia whether gravipack.archemia.fr is theirs and what it hosts. - Keep a domain register with these columns: domain, operator, purpose, relationship to gravipack.com, renewal date. 2. **gravipack.ma: decide its role and follow it through.** - **(a) If it is the Moroccan store,** make it genuinely regional: - prices in MAD, and Moroccan delivery, returns and warranty terms, with a Moroccan legal notice; - aligned model names, or a visible French equivalent (e.g. « Sherpa Peak 50L – équivalent France : Sherpa 45 »); - a shipping promise limited to the markets it actually serves. Then add reciprocal hreflang **only between true equivalent pages**, either in the `<head>` of both sites or in their XML sitemaps: ```html <link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr-FR" href="https://www.gravipack.com/produit/<rome>/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr-MA" href="https://gravipack.ma/<rome>/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://www.gravipack.com/produit/<rome>/" /> ``` Yoast and Rank Math do not output cross-domain hreflang, so use a small `wp_head` snippet or the sitemap method. Validate with a crawler's hreflang report (no missing return tags). Also pick one category base on .ma and 301 the other. - **(b) If it is not a separate market operation,** 301 it to gravipack.com, path by path where equivalents exist and otherwise to the closest category. Keep the domain registered. 3. **gravipacker.com:** - If it is a community or event site, keep it non-commercial, correct the address to the current seat, and link once, clearly, to the official store. - If it is redundant, 301 it to the existing /gravipackers/ testimonials page on gravipack.com. 4. **gravipack.archemia.fr (staging):** - Run `curl -sI https://gravipack.archemia.fr/`. - If it serves a copy of the site, put it behind HTTP Basic Auth. This is the most robust option, because it blocks both crawlers and people: ```apache AuthType Basic AuthName Staging AuthUserFile /chemin/.htpasswd Require valid-user ``` - If authentication is impossible, send `Header set X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow"` for the whole host. - Do not rely on WordPress's 'Demander aux moteurs de recherche de ne pas indexer ce site'. It is a weak control and is often copied to production by mistake. Add a go-live checklist item that makes sure neither that setting nor the authentication reaches the live site. - Search the production database (Better Search Replace, dry run, 'archemia') to confirm that no canonical, hreflang, image or sitemap URL points to the staging host. - If staging pages are ever indexed, verify the host in Search Console and use Removals while the authentication takes effect. 5. **Declare the official domains.** List them in the footer and the mentions légales (« Sites officiels : gravipack.com (France) ; gravipack.ma (Maroc) », if .ma is kept). Keep the Organization JSON-LD `url` on the canonical gravipack.com host. Use `sameAs` for profiles (LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram), not for sister stores. 6. **International (Info).** If English or Spanish sales are ever planned, use subfolders on the canonical host (/en/, /es/) with WPML or Polylang, and self-referencing, reciprocal hreflang that includes x-default. Do not publish machine-translated product pages without review. Until then, no action is needed. The presta redirect plan has its own finding and is not repeated here.

findings.title: #29 Cart, sort and filter parameter URLs appear in the index (?add-to-cart=, ?order=, filter_product_cat=)
findings.description:
Four parameter URLs were among the roughly 114 owned URLs observed in the search results we sampled:
- https://gravipack.com/?add-to-cart=6527, titled 'Accueil - Le sac à dos exosquelette GRAVIPACK anti mal au dos'. The current home title we observed is 'Gravipack : le sac révolutionnaire anti mal de dos exosquelette'.
- https://www.gravipack.com/boutique-gravipack/?add-to-cart=2678 ('Sac a dos exosquelette anti-mal de dos Gravipack qui allège le poids sur les épaules et le dos.').
- https://www.gravipack.com/boutique-gravipack/?order=price ('Boutique Gravipack').
- https://www.gravipack.com/boutique-gravipack/?order=price&filter_product_cat=nouveau-sac-a-dos (107-character title 'Boutique - Sac a dos anti mal de dos GRAVIPACK avec exosquelette allège le poids…').

In the 'gravipack prix' sample, the sort duplicate ?order=price ranked #5, right after the clean /boutique-gravipack/ at #4, and took a brand-query slot.

The titles use old suffixes, which points to old crawl snapshots, so the live site may already handle these URLs. `?order=` and `filter_product_cat=` are not WooCommerce core parameters (core sorting uses `?orderby=`), which suggests a theme or filter widget generates them.

A correction to the earlier version: bot hits on add-to-cart links do **not** affect stock. WooCommerce reserves or reduces stock only at checkout or order, so the only real side effects are analytics and session pollution.

Rated Medium. Downgrade to Low if the live site already noindexes or blocks these states.

Why it matters: An add-to-cart URL is an action, not a page, and a sort or filter state duplicates the listing it modifies. Once indexed, these copies compete with the real home and shop pages and can be picked as the shop's canonical. They also multiply as more filters are added.

Effect on SEO: These URLs waste crawl, create duplicates of the home and shop pages (one of them with an outdated title), and take brand-SERP slots. Bot add-to-cart hits create sessions and carts that distort analytics; they do not affect stock.

Applying noindex in the right order removes these URLs without losing link signals.

Impact 4/10 · Effort Low · Confidence needs-on-site-check
findings.recommendation: 1. **Check the live behaviour** of the four URLs (see onsite_check). If they already send `noindex` (meta robots or X-Robots-Tag), only monitoring is needed. 2. **Add-to-cart links.** - Enable WooCommerce → Réglages → Produits → 'Activer les boutons Ajout au panier en AJAX sur les archives'. - Check that the theme keeps WooCommerce's default `rel="nofollow"` on loop add-to-cart buttons. This is a hint to crawlers, not a block. 3. **Noindex the parameter states with one filter.** Do not also add a canonical pointing to another URL on the same page; choose one signal. Yoast omits the canonical on noindexed URLs; check what Rank Math outputs. ```php // Yoast SEO (code-snippets plugin or child theme) add_filter( 'wpseo_robots', function ( $robots ) { foreach ( array( 'add-to-cart', 'order', 'orderby', 'filter_product_cat', 'min_price', 'max_price' ) as $p ) { if ( isset( $_GET[ $p ] ) ) { return 'noindex, follow'; } } return $robots; } ); // Rank Math equivalent add_filter( 'rank_math/frontend/robots', function ( $robots ) { foreach ( array( 'add-to-cart', 'order', 'orderby', 'filter_product_cat', 'min_price', 'max_price' ) as $p ) { if ( isset( $_GET[ $p ] ) ) { $robots['index'] = 'noindex'; $robots['follow'] = 'follow'; } } return $robots; } ); ``` 4. **Find the widget that creates `?order=` and `filter_product_cat=`.** It may be a theme shop grid, a page-builder product widget, or a filter plugin such as WOOF or YITH. - Enable its 'noindex filtered URLs' option, or render the filters as buttons instead of crawlable links. - For category navigation, link to the clean /categorie-produit/… URLs instead of `?filter_product_cat=`. 5. **Sequencing.** Wait until Search Console shows these URLs as 'Exclue par la balise noindex' and they have left the index. Only then add this to robots.txt: ``` User-agent: * Disallow: /*?add-to-cart= Disallow: /*&add-to-cart= ``` Blocking earlier would stop Google from seeing the noindex. Keep sort and filter URLs crawlable with noindex, unless Crawl stats show heavy waste. 6. **Check** that the XML sitemap and internal links never include parameter URLs, and that parameter URLs on the non-canonical host are covered by the host redirect (see the host finding).

findings.title: #36 Low-value archives and duplicate CMS pages are indexed (attribute/tag archives, a /category/ base, a /test/ copy, duplicate contact pages)
findings.description:
About 8 low-value or duplicate URLs were indexed among the roughly 100 gravipack.com URLs observed in the search results we sampled:
- **WooCommerce attribute archives:** www /attribut-produit/accessoires/exosquelette-gravipack/ ('Archives des Exosquelette Gravipack - Gravipack, le sac à dos …', 109 characters) and /attribut-produit/accessoires/poches-frontales/ (103 characters).
- **Product tag archive:** /etiquette-produit/precommande/ ('Précommande - Sac a dos exosquelette anti-mal de dos Gravipack …', 109 characters).
- **A second blog-category base:** www /category/gravipack-engage-dans-le-handicap-et-l-inclusion/ ('Actualité Handicap - …', 116 characters). It carries the old suffix and may be a stale entry. The main base is /categorie/ (/categorie/innovation/, /categorie/technologie/, /categorie/militaire/, /categorie/outillage/), and those archives use the default title 'X Archives - …' (up to 94 characters).
- **/test/** (www) is indexed with the same title as /gravipack-soulage-les-forces-speciales-au-sofins/ plus the old suffix (122 characters). It looks like a draft copy of the SOFINS post.
- **Two contact URLs:** www /contact-gravipack/ ('Contactez Gravipack') and apex /contacts/ ('Contacts - Le sac à dos exosquelette GRAVIPACK anti mal au dos'). /contacts/ carries the old suffix and may be stale.
- **Two blog listing pages:** /articles/ and /actualites-gravipack-2/. The '-2' only shows that the slug collided with another when the page was created; it does not prove that a sibling page still exists.

Corrections to the earlier version:
- Paginated /page/2/ URLs are **not** a problem; they should stay indexable with a self-referencing canonical.
- 'Thin' would require word and product counts we do not have, so these pages are described as low-value.
- The claim that the Innovation and Militaire archives list the same posts is unsupported and has been dropped.
- The two RATP posts, and /nos-engagements/ versus /a-propos-de-nous-gravipack-au-service-de-votre-dos/, can be legitimately distinct and are not counted as duplicates.
- /devis/ versus /devis-gravipack/ is covered in the B2B finding.

About 8 URLs on a site of about 100 is Low.

Why it matters: Archive pages that only re-list a handful of products, and leftover test or duplicate pages, give searchers nothing new. They dilute site-quality signals, use crawl budget, and can appear in place of the real page: /test/ could be shown instead of the SOFINS post, or a stale /contacts/ could show old details. Duplicate contact URLs also split the 'who you are and how to reach you' signals that Google looks for on a merchant site.

Effect on SEO: The effects are minor index bloat, a possible wrong-URL choice for the SOFINS post and the contact page, and long templated 'Archives' titles in the results. Cleaning these up concentrates signals on the real category, post and contact pages. The ranking impact is small.

Impact 3/10 · Effort Low · Confidence needs-on-site-check
findings.recommendation: 1. **Check status first** (see onsite_check). URLs that already return 301 or 404 are stale index entries and need nothing. 2. **/test/:** if it returns 200, 301 it to /gravipack-soulage-les-forces-speciales-au-sofins/ (Redirection, or Rank Math → Redirections). Then delete the test post and empty the Corbeille. If you want to keep it as a working draft, set it to Brouillon or Privé so it stops resolving publicly. 3. **Contact pages:** keep the one used in the menu on the canonical host (likely /contact-gravipack/), and 301 /contacts/ to it, plus /contact/ if that exists. Do not create a new contact URL. The contact details themselves (legal entity, current seat) are handled in the entity-facts finding. 4. **Product attribute and tag archives.** Set them to noindex with one of these: - Yoast (v20+): Paramètres → Catégories et étiquettes → 'Étiquettes produits' and each 'Attribut produit (pa_…)' → turn off 'Afficher … dans les résultats de recherche' (labels vary by version). - Rank Math: Titres et métas → Étiquettes produits / attributs → Robots meta = No Index. - Or remove the archives entirely: Produits → Attributs → edit → untick 'Activer les archives ?'. Then 301 any archive URL that has links to the matching category. 5. **Blog categories:** keep /categorie/innovation/, /technologie/, /militaire/ and /outillage/ indexable only if each gets a short, unique intro and lists enough posts; otherwise set them to noindex,follow. Replace the default 'Archives' title template with `%%term_title%% %%sep%% %%sitename%%` (Yoast) or `%term% %sep% %sitename%` (Rank Math). This is shared with the title-template finding. 6. **/category/ base:** - Confirm that Réglages → Permaliens → 'Préfixe des catégories' is set to 'categorie'. - If /category/… still answers 200, 301 it to the matching /categorie/… archive with a Redirection regex (`^/category/(.*)` → `/categorie/$1`), but only where the slugs match. - Map the handicap archive to its existing /categorie/ equivalent, or to the post it lists. 7. **Blog index:** - Check which page is set as the 'Page des articles' under Réglages → Lecture. Keep that one, and 301 the other listing only if it is a true duplicate. - Before renaming /actualites-gravipack-2/, look in Pages → Corbeille for an 'actualites-gravipack' item that blocks the clean slug. - Any rename gets a 301 and goes into the single migration map. 8. **Leave pagination alone** (/boutique-gravipack/page/2/, /categorie-produit/…/page/2/): self-canonical, indexable, with plain `<a href>` links. Confirm that the Yoast or Rank Math sitemap drops the noindexed taxonomies; both plugins do this automatically.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every product and category page carries a descriptive, French, intent-bearing title
Use-case categories already exist (randonnée, scolaire, business, militaire, médical, outillage) — the outillage hub already ranks for a generic head term

findings.title: #6 Segment categories rank mainly for 'anti mal de dos' wordings and miss the market's generic head terms (sac à dos ergonomique, cartable ergonomique, sac randonnée léger…)
findings.description:
The structure is already in place: 10 segment sub-categories exist under /categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/ (randonnée, scolaire, business/télétravail, voyage, urbain, médical, militaire/tactique, outillage, claie de portage, nouveaux). The problem is what they are named after: the brand's technology and benefit ('exosquelette', 'anti mal de dos'), not the generic words the market searches with.

Category titles as indexed:
- Randonnée: 'Sac à dos exosquelette de randonnée anti-mal de dos et anti-TMS'
- Scolaire: 'Sac à dos exosquelette scolaire Gravipack allège le poids de 92%'
- Business: 'Sac à dos exosquelette anti-mal de dos business voyage d'affaires'
- Urbain: 'Sac à dos exosquelette urbain Gravipack allege le poids sur le dos'
- Médical: 'Sac à dos médical Gravipack allégez vos missions sauvez des vies'
- Militaire: 'Sac à dos exosquelette militaire d'assault allège le poids Gravipack'
- Claie: 'Claie de portage Gravipack anti-TMS pour charges très lourdes'
- Parent hub: 'Achetez un sac à dos révolutionnaire avec exosquelette Gravipack'
Category slugs run 90-151 characters.

Where they rank. These are extended-mode results from the search results we sampled (a US-located, non-Google index); positions are directional.
- With the 'anti mal de dos' feature modifier, gravipack.com does rank:
  - 'sac à dos scolaire anti mal de dos': #1-#3 (two Kingston product pages and the scolaire category)
  - 'sac à dos ergonomique mal de dos': #2 and #4 (Hiking 30 L Gris, home page)
  - 'sac à dos anti mal de dos': #4-#6
  - 'sac à dos randonnée anti mal de dos': #5-#6 (randonnée category, home page)
  - 'sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique anti mal de dos': #3-#5 (Business Talk V4 25 L, business category, home page)
- The exception that proves the model: the outillage hub ranks #9 for the generic 'sac à dos porte-outils', behind ManoMano, Leboncoin, DeWalt, Leroy Merlin, Hellopro, Rubix, OPPBTP and Fischer Darex. A second run reproduced this identically. Its title now reads 'Sac à dos exosquelette pour l'outillage professionnel Gravipack', which uses the market's words and has no 'anti mal de dos'.
- Absent for the generic wordings:
  - 'sac à dos ergonomique': sacados.fr, mon-sac-a-dos.fr, karkoa, sacroche, la-sacoche-officielle, accergo, le-repaire-du-sac-a-dos, arsayo, ma-boutique-ergonomique. Six of the nine are collection or product pages named after the query. Standard mode (osprey, manor, ergobag, deuter) showed no Gravipack either.
  - 'cartable ergonomique': lespetitsbaroudeurs (ergobag + a category), mon-sac-a-dos, mahilana, ma-boutique-ergonomique ×4, univers-cartable. It shares 0 URLs with 'sac à dos scolaire anti mal de dos', so it is a separate set of results.
  - 'sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique': mon-sac-a-dos, Eastpak, Darty, Ergonovie.
  - 'sac à dos médical secouriste': Girodmedical, SMSP, Praxisdienst.
  - 'sac à dos militaire tactique léger': Projet13, Mode-Tactique, V8.
- Likely absent (standard mode or single runs only):
  - 'sac à dos randonnée léger ergonomique' (deuter ×4, alpinstore ×3, glisshop)
  - 'sac à dos randonnée 60+10' (deuter, alpinstore, tonton-outdoor, alltricks), although Helsinki and Oslo are 60+10 L
  - 'sac à dos voyage ergonomique' (deuter Voyager ×7, osprey, thule)
  - 'claie de portage ergonomique' (alpinstore, tonton-outdoor)
  - 'sac à dos Compostelle mal de dos' (conseilsport.decathlon.fr, pilgrim sites), although Compostelle products exist and 'compostelle' is in the randonnée slug
  - 'sac à dos vélotaf ergonomique' (tonton-outdoor, culturevelo)
- 'Sac à dos ergonomique' appears in the titles of the Centurion, Kingston and Dublin product pages and of /mentions-legales/, but in no category title.

School nuance: the 'cartable ergonomique' results are led by primary-school cartables (ergobag Prime 'cartable CP primaire', univers-cartable). Gravipack's scolaire category targets collège, lycée and étudiants (per its slug), and its school products (Kingston, G-Pack 'collège-lycée') are backpacks. 'Cartable' is an adjacent segment and should be used only where it describes the product accurately.

Realistic upside: head-term results are dominated by Deuter, Osprey, military.eu and large retailers. The likely gain is in the mid-tail and in moving from page 2 to page 1, as the outillage hub shows, rather than a top-3 position for 'sac à dos ergonomique'.

Why it matters: For commercial category queries, the page type that wins is a category or collection page whose title and H1 name the category the way searchers do. Buyers search by activity plus feature ('sac à dos randonnée ergonomique', 'sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique', 'sac à dos porte-outils', 'sac à dos médical') and compare specifications.

Hubs written only around the brand's own vocabulary catch the 'anti mal de dos' long tail and miss most of each segment's demand, even though the products fit those queries.

Effect on SEO: Adding the market head term to each category's title, H1 and intro, while keeping 'anti mal de dos' as a secondary term, should extend category visibility beyond the modifier long tail. It should reach mid-tail and some head queries in randonnée, business, scolaire, médical and militaire, as already happened for outillage.

Spec-rich buying-guide copy (volume, empty weight, laptop size, strap sizes) also matches the comparison vocabulary that competitors and AI answers use.

Impact 6/10 · Effort Medium · Confidence likely
findings.recommendation: 1. Size the opportunity first. - Pull French volumes and difficulty (Google Keyword Planner or DataForSEO, location France) for: 'sac à dos ergonomique', 'cartable ergonomique', 'sac à dos scolaire ergonomique', 'sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique', 'sac à dos randonnée ergonomique', 'sac à dos porte-outils', 'sac à dos médical', 'sac à dos tactique', 'claie de portage', 'sac à dos vélotaf'. - Add GSC impressions per category. - Prioritise the 2-3 segments with the best combination of volume and product fit. 2. Do not rename the parent slug 'tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette'. WooCommerce category URLs are hierarchical, so a rename changes about 12 child URLs, as well as the URL that currently ranks for 'sac à dos exosquelette'. - For 'sac à dos ergonomique', start by giving the existing hub a title and H1 that carry both terms. Use the same wording as the cannibalisation fix: title 'Sac à dos ergonomique à exosquelette, anti mal de dos | Gravipack', H1 'Sacs à dos ergonomiques à exosquelette, anti mal de dos'. - Only if the hub still gets no impressions for 'sac à dos ergonomique' after 8-12 weeks, create a separate landing page or top-level category 'Sacs à dos ergonomiques'. Give it a distinct angle (comparison by use) so it does not duplicate the hub. 3. Retitle each segment category as market term + differentiator + brand. Add the generic term and keep 'anti mal de dos' where the category already ranks with it. Change the category Name in Produits → Catégories and the SEO title; keep the slug. Character counts in brackets: - Randonnée: 'Sac à dos randonnée ergonomique anti mal de dos | Gravipack' (59) - Business: 'Sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique anti mal de dos | Gravipack' (60) - Scolaire: 'Sac à dos scolaire ergonomique à exosquelette | Gravipack' (57). Add 'cartable' to the copy only for models suited to primary school, if there are any. - Outillage (already ranks #9): light touch only, e.g. 'Sac à dos porte-outils pro à exosquelette | Gravipack' (53). Test this change on its own, and do not change the URL. - Médical: 'Sac à dos médical et secouriste ergonomique | Gravipack' (55) - Militaire: 'Sac à dos tactique militaire ergonomique | Gravipack' (52). This also fixes the 'assault' typo. - Voyage: 'Sac à dos de voyage ergonomique à exosquelette | Gravipack' (58) - Urbain: 'Sac à dos urbain et vélotaf ergonomique | Gravipack' (51), but only if the bike-suited models (Tokyo, Rome) are in this category. - Claie: 'Claie de portage ergonomique, charges lourdes | Gravipack' (57). Drop 'anti-TMS' until the claims review decides. Make each H1 the category name, carrying the same head term. 4. Copy for each category. claude-seo's category gate is 400+ words; Google sets no word count. - Above the grid, 50-120 words: what the category is, who it is for, and the differentiator. - Below the grid, 400-600 words: a spec comparison table across the models (volume, empty weight, max load, laptop size, rain cover, strap sizes M-XXL), sizing advice, real use cases, and links to guides. - Add a 'Compostelle' H2 to the randonnée category. - Example intro for randonnée: « Nos sacs à dos de randonnée ergonomiques intègrent un exosquelette breveté qui répartit la charge entre le dos et les épaules. Du sac à la journée au sac de trek 60+10 L, choisissez selon la durée de vos sorties, le volume et la taille de vos bretelles. » 5. If attribute filters are added (usage, volume, ordinateur), keep filter combinations out of the index with one method only: either noindex,follow or a canonical to the base category, not both. 6. Slugs: change category slugs only for hubs that do not rank, and only inside the single URL migration release, with 1:1 301s. Do not toggle Rank Math's 'Remove product category base' (Rank Math → General Settings → WooCommerce) outside that release: it changes every category URL. 7. Structured data: CollectionPage + ItemList + BreadcrumbList on each category (see the cannibalisation finding). 8. Track these terms in a France/Google.fr rank tracker (mobile): 'sac à dos porte-outils', 'sac à dos ergonomique', 'sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique', 'sac à dos scolaire ergonomique', 'sac à dos médical secouriste', 'sac à dos randonnée ergonomique'.

findings.title: #9 Dozens of pages target the same 'anti mal de dos' and 'exosquelette' terms, so the home page, category hub and product pages compete
findings.description:
The repetition is real. These counts come from titles and URLs as indexed in the search results we sampled (a US-located, non-Google index):
- 53 of 98 gravipack.com titles contain 'anti mal de dos', 'anti-mal de dos' or 'anti mal au dos'.
- 28 of 39 product titles contain it, and 37 slugs contain 'anti-mal-de-dos'.
- 66 of 98 titles contain 'exosquelette'.
- The site-wide title suffix adds both terms to 13 more pages.
- At least 11 URLs target 'sac (à dos) randonnée anti mal de dos' by title or slug: the randonnée category, Sherpa bleu ('Sac randonnée léger anti mal de dos exosquelette bretelles Sherpa'), Pearl ('Sac randonner léger…'), Easy Travel and Helsinki (slug 'sac-randonner-leger-anti-mal-de-dos'), Compostelle 80 L ('…randonnée 80L révolutionnaire anti mal de dos pas cher'), Oslo Rouge, Hiking Terracotta, Hiking Gris, Sherpa Kaki, and presta /24-sac-a-dos-sport.
- The same models also exist under several URLs: G-Pack ×2, Light Promax ×3, Business Talk V4 ×3, Cargo Max ×2, Kingston ×2, and Sherpa Kaki on both /produit/ and /produit-gravipack/. This is the clearest source of competing URLs and is handled in the duplicate-product finding.

What the sampled results show. These are extended-mode results; positions are directional and come from single runs, and standard mode disagreed.
- 'sac à dos anti mal de dos': gravipack.com held 3 of 9 results (Pearl product page, home page, Tokyo product page). ergo-corner.com, a reseller of Gravipack, held 3 more, and an ici.fr piece about Gravipack 1, so 7 of the 9 results relate to Gravipack. In standard mode no gravipack.com URL appeared; decathlon.fr/vc/gravipack did.
- 'sac à dos randonnée anti mal de dos': the randonnée category ranked about #5 and the home page about #6, so the intended category does rank.
- 'sac à dos porte-outils anti mal de dos': 5 Gravipack URLs in the top 10 (ExoTool, Light Promax ×2, ToolMaster, outillage category). That is domination of the results, not proof of harm.
- 'sac à dos scolaire anti mal de dos': two Kingston URLs and the scolaire category hold #1-#3.
- 'sac à dos exosquelette': the main category and the home page both appear, at about #6-#7.
- The existing hub, /categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/, is not the URL that ranks for 'sac à dos anti mal de dos'; the home page and single product pages are. The hub is titled 'Achetez un sac à dos révolutionnaire avec exosquelette Gravipack' (page 2: 'Tous les sacs à dos anti-mal de dos exosquelette Gravipack') and has 10 segment sub-categories.
- The three 'anti mal de dos' query variants share 4 URLs pairwise. But those are the most ubiquitous URLs in the whole data set (ergo-corner/55, ergo-corner/13, arsayo, the home page). Without ergo-corner the overlap drops to 2, which calls for interlinking the pages, not for one page serving all three queries.

What is not shown: that rankings are diluted or rotating. Several URLs from one site in a results page is extra visibility. Real cannibalisation, meaning URLs alternating for one query and splitting its impressions, can only be confirmed in Search Console.

Why it matters: When dozens of pages present the same primary term, the engine, not the site, decides which URL answers each query.

For broad category intent ('sac à dos anti mal de dos', 'sac à dos exosquelette'), the page type that usually wins is a category page with buying-guide content. A product page covers one model, and the home page is navigational.

If the hub is not clearly signposted as the answer, links and engagement stay spread across the home page and individual products. Then the page best suited to the brand's main phrase cannot build up its strength.

Effect on SEO: Concentrating the head terms on the existing hub (title, H1, copy, internal anchors), while product pages lead with use + model, should make one URL the stable answer for each head query. Product pages then capture the long tail.

If GSC shows URLs alternating, consolidation reduces position swings and recovers clicks lost to the wrong landing page, for example a 60 L trekking bag shown for a commuter query. If GSC shows no alternation, the gain is smaller and comes mostly from the hub's better relevance.

Impact 6/10 · Effort Medium · Confidence likely
findings.recommendation: 1. Confirm in Search Console first. That is Google.fr data; this audit's positions come from a different engine. - Go to Performance → Search results, add a Query filter (contains) for 'anti mal de dos', and open the Pages tab. - Repeat for 'sac à dos exosquelette', 'randonnée anti mal de dos', 'scolaire anti mal de dos' and 'porte outils'. - Cannibalisation means two or more URLs each take a meaningful share of impressions for the same query, with positions alternating week to week. To see this, compare date ranges, or use Looker Studio with the GSC connector (query + page by week). - If one URL already takes more than about 80 % of a query's impressions, leave that query alone. 2. Build a keyword-to-URL map in one sheet with columns: query | intent | target URL | allowed secondary URLs | internal anchor. - Existing hub /categorie-produit/tous-les-sacs-a-dos-exosquelette/ → 'sac à dos anti mal de dos' + 'sac à dos exosquelette' (+ 'sac à dos ergonomique'; see the category head-terms finding) - Home page → brand terms ('Gravipack', 'sac à dos Gravipack') + 'sac à dos exosquelette'. Keep 'anti mal de dos' in the home title until the hub ranks. - Randonnée category → 'sac à dos randonnée anti mal de dos / ergonomique' - Scolaire category → 'sac à dos scolaire anti mal de dos' - Business category → 'sac à dos ordinateur ergonomique anti mal de dos' - Outillage → 'sac à dos porte-outils'; Claie → 'claie de portage' - Product pages → use + model + capacity, with 'anti mal de dos' as a secondary modifier. 3. Retarget the existing hub. Do not create a new /sac-a-dos-anti-mal-de-dos/ URL; that would add yet another competing page. - Title: 'Sac à dos ergonomique à exosquelette, anti mal de dos | Gravipack' (65 characters; only the brand falls in the cut-off zone). - H1: 'Sacs à dos ergonomiques à exosquelette, anti mal de dos'. - Both are subject to the health-claims wording decision. - Add an 80-150-word intro above the product grid: what the exoskeleton does and who each segment is for. - Put the longer buying guide below the grid: how to choose by use, volume and strap size (M-XXL), with links to each segment category. - To print bottom-of-category text from a term meta field, add to the child theme: add_action( 'woocommerce_after_shop_loop', function () { if ( ! is_product_category() ) { return; } $term = get_queried_object(); $html = get_term_meta( $term->term_id, 'seo_bottom_text', true ); if ( $html ) { echo '<section class="cat-guide">' . wp_kses_post( wpautop( $html ) ) . '</section>'; } }, 20 ); 4. Stage the change in this order: a. Publish the hub copy and the internal links. b. Wait 4-6 weeks and re-check GSC. c. Only then make the home title brand-led and move product titles to use + model. Never strip 'anti mal de dos' from all product titles at once: the audit found those titles currently earn long-tail visibility. 5. Internal links. These are the strongest signal the site controls. - Add a main menu item 'Sacs à dos anti mal de dos' pointing to the hub. Link the home hero and category tiles to the hub and the segment categories with descriptive anchors. - On every product page, enable breadcrumbs (Yoast, Rank Math or WooCommerce) and add one contextual link to its segment category, e.g. 'Voir tous nos sacs de randonnée à exosquelette'. - Blog posts should link to categories, not to random products. - The exact anchor 'sac à dos anti mal de dos' points only to the hub. 6. Consolidate same-model duplicates (G-Pack, Light Promax, Business Talk V4, Cargo Max, Kingston) as described in the duplicate-product finding. If the 'Vive la rentrée scolaire' Kingston URL is the same product as the main Kingston URL, 301 it there. 7. Structured data on the hub: CollectionPage + ItemList + BreadcrumbList, not Article. - Yoast and Rank Math already output CollectionPage and BreadcrumbList for product categories in their @graph. Add only the ItemList, via the wpseo_schema_graph or rank_math/json_ld filter, so the page keeps a single graph. For example: {"@type":"ItemList","itemListElement":[{"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"url":"https://gravipack.com/produit/<sherpa-45>/"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"url":"https://gravipack.com/produit/<oslo-60-10>/"}]} - Use the canonical host decided in the host fix. 8. Repeat step 1 eight weeks after each stage.

findings.title: #11 Title tags are over-long, carry a bloated site-wide suffix and stacked claim keywords, and sometimes omit the model name or contain typos
findings.description:
Source: the titles of 114 URLs (98 on gravipack.com / www.gravipack.com and 16 on the legacy presta.gravipack.com) as they were displayed in the search results we sampled. These came from a US-located, non-Google index. Displayed titles can differ from the raw <title>, so every number below needs an on-site check.

1. Length. 76 of the 98 gravipack.com titles exceed 60 characters (median 65; 29 exceed 80). Including presta, the figure is 87 of 114. One counted title (the RATP post) ends in '...', so its length is a lower bound. The extremes:
- Compostelle 65 L: 204 characters. Compostelle 25 L and 35 L: 182.
- The post /cest-une-veritable-revolution-pour-le-marche-colossal-du-sac-dos/: 154.
- Helsinki: 136 ('Sac à dos GRAVIPACK exosquelette 60+10 L : soulage le dos et les épaules, répartit la charge. Recommandé pour randonnée et port prolongé'). This is a description pasted into the title field.
- /test/ 122, Kingston 118, /category/gravipack-engage-dans-le-handicap-et-l-inclusion/ 116, Dublin 101, Tokyo 95, Sherpa Kaki 90, Hiking Terracotta 90, Austerlitz 85.
- The home page title is 63 characters ('Gravipack : le sac révolutionnaire anti mal de dos exosquelette') in the main snapshot. It is not a product title.

2. Bloated site-wide suffix. 13 URLs end in ' - Gravipack, le sac à dos exosquelette anti-mal de dos homme femme enfant' (73 characters): Compostelle 25/35/65 L, /gravipackers/, /articles/, /test/, the 'révolution' post, /categorie/innovation/, /categorie/technologie/, /categorie/militaire/, /categorie-produit/accessoires-sac-a-dos/ and two /attribut-produit/ archives. Search engines shorten titles; they do not lengthen them. So this is almost certainly the live title template (the site name or tagline fed into the site-name variable). At least two templates were observed. Other URLs end in ' - Sac a dos exosquelette anti-mal de dos Gravipack qui allège le poids sur les épaules et le dos.' (/etiquette-produit/precommande/, the /category/…handicap archive) or in ' - Le sac à dos exosquelette GRAVIPACK anti mal au dos' (/contacts/, /devis/). These may come from older crawl snapshots.

3. Default archive wording is still in use: 'Innovation Archives', 'Technologie Archives', 'Militaire Archives', 'Outillage Archives', 'Accessoires sac à dos Archives', 'Archives des Exosquelette Gravipack', 'Archives des Poches frontales'. These are the English and French defaults of the SEO plugin's taxonomy template.

4. Model names are missing, or sit at characters 46-68, where the title is cut off.
- No model name: Oslo Rouge ('Sac ergonomique de randonnée anti-mal de dos avec exosquelette', which also has no brand), Centurion ('Sac à dos ergonomique anti-mal de dos avec exosquelette Gravipack'), ToolMaster ('Sac outillage anti-mal de dos exosquelette'), both Business Talk V4 25 L URLs ('Sac à dos exosquelette 25L anti-mal de dos pour deux ordinateurs' and 'Sac à dos ordinateur 25L anti-mal de dos révolutionnaire'), and Gravitech/Barracuda ('Claie de portage révolutionnaire exosquelette anti-mal de dos').
- No brand: Sherpa bleu ('Sac randonnée léger anti mal de dos exosquelette bretelles Sherpa') and Oslo.
- Identical titles on different URLs: G-Pack ×2, Light Promax ×2 ('Sac à dos outillage anti-douleur exosquelette Gravipack®'), Cargo Max ×2, Sherpa Kaki ×3. The duplicate URLs themselves are covered in the duplicate-product finding.

5. Typos. These were verbatim at crawl time. Search engines do not introduce typos, but some may have been fixed since.
- 'Sac randonner léger … Pearl': 'randonner' is the verb; it should be 'randonnée'.
- 'militaire d'assault' (militaire category): should be 'd'assaut'.
- 'allege' (urbain category): should be 'allège'.
- 'Sac a dos' (Dublin, a shop filter URL, the Précommande tag, presta): should be 'Sac à dos'.
- 'ce sac à dos allègent' (presta home): should be 'allège'.
- Lowercase starts: 'fabrication professionnelle…' and 'gravipack' (Rome: 'Sac anti mal de dos business ROME ergonomique gravipack').
- Brand casing varies: Gravipack / GRAVIPACK / GraviPack® / Gravipack®.

6. Thin or off-target titles:
- 'Boutique Gravipack' (18 characters; on the shop, its /page/2/ and ?order=price), 'Contactez Gravipack' (19), 'Nos engagements' (15).
- /mentions-legales/: 'Le sac à dos ergonomique - Mentions légales, tout ce que vous devez savoir sur Gravipack.' (89).
- A seasonal 'Vive la rentrée scolaire…' title on an evergreen Kingston product page.

7. Stacked claim tokens:
- 'révolutionnaire' in about 10 titles (home, main category, G-Pack ×2, City, Business Talk V4 ×2, Compostelle 80 L, Gravitech…)
- 'anti douleur' / 'anti-douleur' (Sherpa Kaki, Light Promax ×2)
- 'anti-TMS' (randonnée and claie categories)
- '92%' (scolaire category, one post)
- 'apesanteur' (6, mostly presta)
- 'meilleur' and 'Le seul sac à dos au monde' (presta)
The health-claims finding decides what wording is allowed. This finding covers length, template and format.

Not claimed: that Google is rewriting these titles (the index sampled is not Google), or that the home page has two titles (one of them belonged to a ?add-to-cart= parameter URL).

What already works: several category titles are close to the target length. Outillage is 63 characters ('Sac à dos exosquelette pour l'outillage professionnel Gravipack'), claie de portage 61, 'Tous les sacs à dos anti-mal de dos exosquelette Gravipack' 58, and /faq/ 58.

Why it matters: The title is the headline of every organic result and the strongest on-page hint of what a page is about. claude-seo's quality gate asks for 30-60 characters, the primary keyword near the start, the brand last, and a unique title per page.

Google cuts titles by pixel width (about 580-600 px, roughly 55-65 characters). On most Gravipack product pages, that cut falls before the model name and capacity, which are what a buyer who already knows the range types ('gravipack sherpa', 'gravipack oslo 60+10'). As a result, every result reads like its siblings: 'Sac … anti mal de dos … exosquelette …'.

The 73-character tagline repeats 'exosquelette anti-mal de dos' on every templated page. This adds to the site-wide keyword repetition and makes legal, archive and test pages present themselves on the same words as products.

Typos and stacked superlatives ('révolutionnaire', 'anti douleur') sit in the most visible line of the snippet. That hurts trust with a French audience that is already sceptical in the forum and review results.

Effect on SEO: The effect is mainly on CTR and relevance, not on indexing.
- Shorter titles with the model near the start show the model, capacity and use in full. This helps model queries, where marketplaces and resellers currently outrank gravipack.com, and click-through on long-tail queries.
- Removing the suffix cuts site-wide keyword repetition, and stops archive and utility pages from presenting themselves as product pages.
- Over-long or boilerplate titles invite engines to rewrite them, which reduces control over the message.

Under claude-seo, title length is a CTR issue rather than an eligibility issue, hence Medium.

Impact 6/10 · Effort Medium · Confidence likely
findings.recommendation: Stage 0 – Baseline (before any change) 1. Export the current titles from Screaming Frog (Page Titles tab → Export) or from the Yoast/Rank Math bulk editor. 2. Export GSC Performance → Pages for the last 3 months (clicks, impressions, CTR, position) for all product, category and post URLs. Keep both files as the baseline. Stage 1 – Remove the suffix at template level (day 1, low risk) 3. Find where the tagline comes from. It is usually the WordPress Site Title (Réglages → Général) or the SEO plugin's site name. Menu labels vary by plugin version. - Yoast v20+: Yoast SEO → Settings → Site basics. Set Website name = 'Gravipack' and choose '|' or '–' as the separator. - Rank Math: set the separator in Titles & Meta → Global Meta and the website name in Titles & Meta → Local SEO. - Setting the site name to 'Gravipack' also gives Google a clean WebSite name. - The slogan can stay as the WordPress tagline, but it must not appear in any title template (%%sitedesc%% / %sitedesc%). 4. Set the templates (Yoast → Settings → Content types / Categories & tags; Rank Math → Titles & Meta): - Products: %%title%% %%sep%% %%sitename%% (Rank Math: %title% %sep% %sitename%) - Product categories: %%term_title%% %%page%% %%sep%% %%sitename%% (Rank Math: %term% %page% %sep% %sitename%) - Posts: %%title%% %%sep%% %%sitename%% - Post categories: %%term_title%% – Actualités %%page%% %%sep%% %%sitename%% - Product tags and attribute archives: %%term_title%% %%sep%% %%sitename%% (whether they stay indexed is handled in the thin-archive finding). Remove 'Archives' and 'Archives des' everywhere. Do not use %%primary_category%% in the product template: the category names are long and would bring back titles of 80+ characters. 5. Check that no page has the tagline hard-coded in its own SEO title field. Take a backup, then run in phpMyAdmin or WP-CLI: SELECT post_id, meta_value FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key IN ('_yoast_wpseo_title','rank_math_title') AND meta_value LIKE '%homme femme enfant%'; Also confirm that the theme declares add_theme_support('title-tag') and does not print its own <title>, and that only one SEO plugin is active. Stage 2 – Typos and thin titles (week 1) 6. Fix the typos: 'randonnée' (not 'randonner'), 'd'assaut', 'allège', 'Sac à dos', 'allègent' → 'allège', and capitalise the first letter of each title. Use one brand spelling in titles, 'Gravipack'; keep ® for body copy only. 7. Rewrite the thin or off-target titles (character counts in brackets): - Shop: 'Boutique sacs à dos à exosquelette | Gravipack' (46) - Contact: 'Contact et devis entreprise | Gravipack' (39) - Engagements: 'Nos engagements : dos, santé, inclusion | Gravipack' (51) - Legal: 'Mentions légales | Gravipack' (28) - CGV: 'Conditions générales de vente | Gravipack' (41) - Kingston: remove 'Vive la rentrée scolaire' from the evergreen title and use a seasonal banner instead. Stage 3 – Product titles (after the keyword map in the cannibalisation finding and the health-claims wording decision) 8. Format: [use term] + [model + capacity/colour] + [differentiator] | Gravipack. - Keep it to 60 characters or fewer. - Put the model within the first ~35 characters so it is never cut off. - The use term stays first because model names have little search demand of their own (claude-seo: primary keyword near the start). - Keep 'anti mal de dos' as a secondary modifier where the claims decision allows it. Do not strip it from every product title before the category hub ranks for it. Examples: - 'Sac de randonnée Sherpa 45 L à exosquelette | Gravipack' (55) - 'Sac de trek Oslo 60+10 L rouge, anti mal de dos | Gravipack' (59) - 'Sac à dos ordinateur Business Talk V4 25 L | Gravipack' (54) - 'Sac porte-outils ToolMaster à exosquelette | Gravipack' (54) - 'Sac à dos ergonomique Centurion à exosquelette | Gravipack' (58) - 'Sac de voyage Pearl 29 L anti mal de dos | Gravipack' (52) - 'Sac à dos urbain Austerlitz à exosquelette | Gravipack' (54) - 'Sac de trek Compostelle 65 L ergonomique | Gravipack' (52) - 'Sac à dos de trek Helsinki 60+10 L | Gravipack' (46) For the claie, confirm the current model name first: the URL says Gravitech, the copy says Barracuda. 9. The product name is the H1 and also feeds the Merchant Center feed. It can stay model-first and descriptive, e.g. 'Gravipack Sherpa 45 L – Sac de randonnée à exosquelette'. Set the SEO title separately in the Yoast/Rank Math box. 10. Roll out in two batches. Do 10 products first and compare their CTR and impressions with the baseline after 4 weeks, then do the rest. Tools: Yoast SEO → Tools → Bulk editor, the SEO title column on Rank Math's Products list, or a CSV import (WP All Import). Stage 4 – Posts 11. Editorial H1s can stay expressive. Give each post its own SEO title of 60 characters or fewer, starting with the 154-character 'révolution' post and /test/ (which should be removed; see the duplicate-pages finding). Stage 5 – QA 12. Re-crawl with Screaming Frog and check Page Titles → Over 60 characters / Over 561 pixels / Duplicate / Below 30 characters. Targets: - zero duplicates; - zero titles containing 'homme femme enfant' or 'Archives'; - fewer than 10 % of indexable URLs over 60 characters.

findings.title: #12 B2B and occupational (TMS/QVT) demand has no indexable hub; the offers sit inside product pages and service 'products'
findings.description:
Three site-restricted searches in the search results we sampled found no /entreprises/, /professionnels/, CSE, QVT, collectivités, pompiers/secours or prévention-TMS page on gravipack.com. Here is what exists instead.

Quote pages
- /devis/: titled 'Devis - Le sac à dos exosquelette GRAVIPACK anti mal au dos'. B2B team, reply within 24 h, free mock-up; the form asks for the company name and SIRET.
- /devis-gravipack/: titled 'Demandez votre devis Gravipack…', with custom solutions per industry.
- That these two pages serve the same intent is inferred from their titles only.

B2B services published as WooCommerce products
- /produit/fabrication-professionnelle-gravipack/, titled 'fabrication professionnelle, cadeaux d'entreprise et objets publicitaires haut de gamme.' (88 characters, starting in lowercase).
- A key ring carrying the SNCF logo: /produit/porte-cle-flamme-personnalise-avec-logo-sncf-broderie-premium-gravipack/.
- A payment-link product, /produit/lien-de-paiement-unique-pour-votre-commande-personnalisee-gravipack/, which surfaced for CGV and refund queries.
- The waist-belt buckle is a real spare part and is fine as a product.

B2B selling points that exist only inside product sheets
- 'adopté par plus de 120 clients B2B et B2G'
- 'déployé dans entreprises et administrations pour prévenir les TMS et améliorer la QVT'
- prescription by doctors or the médecin du travail
- funding via AGEFIPH / FIPHFP / MDPH / Escavie (ExoTool and others)
- 'tarifs dégressifs pour entreprises & administrations' (Austerlitz)
- prices for collectivités (Centurion)
- SAMU and military doctors
- The home page lists the Armée de Terre, the Légion étrangère, the Préfecture de police, the gendarmerie, fire services and regional councils as users (self-reported).

B2B proof written as news, not as landing pages
- /le-porte-outils-anti-mal-de-dos-gravipack-soulage-les-agents-ratp/, the VivaTech/Le Parisien post, /gravipack-soulage-les-forces-speciales-au-sofins/ (plus a /test/ copy) and the Techterre post.
- RATP Group's own pages name Gravipack. Its CSR page describes an exoskeleton backpack for staff who inspect tracks on foot, and its VivaTech 2023 pages say about 50 roaming maintenance workers were equipped. An owned post says 250 agents, so the figure must be reconciled before it is reused.

Facts that conflict
- The custom-logo key ring shows a minimum order of 20 units on one sheet and 30 on the other.
- Capacity is '20 à 100 litres' on the Techterre post and '20 à 60 litres' on the SOFINS post. These may describe different product families (one post presents the Barracuda claie), so verify.
